_comment: PERF-ROG / OP23-01. Every per-frame performance lever the Meadows chapter has, in one place, so an owner playing on the ROG Ally can turn one without a rebuild. Read by scripts/world/performance_config.gd. ALL TUNABLE. Measured baselines for each are in ralph/PERF_ROG_REPORT.md; re-measure with tools/perf_profile.gd after changing anything here.
_comment_interaction: interaction_grid_cell_m: edge of the uniform x/z grid interaction_arbiter.gd files prompt providers into, metres. The arbiter used to poll all 24,461 registered providers every frame (15.6ms/frame measured on this corridor) to find the two within reach; it now walks only the cells around the player. Cell size trades cells-walked against providers-per-cell and wants to be in the same order as the largest prompt radius (4.0m today). Correctness does not depend on it.
_comment_collision_streaming: vegetation.gd streams real CollisionShape3D nodes in around the player for the scattered trees, rocks and saplings. collision_stream_radius_m is the bubble; collision_stream_interval_s is how often playground_world.gd re-centres it; collision_stream_cell_m is the grid the sweep walks instead of every solid placement in the world. Measured before the grid: 9.2ms per sweep over 22,306 solid placements, twice a second -- a judder rather than a frame-rate floor, but a judder the player feels twice a second.
_comment_scatter_lod: scatter_lod_ranges applies each vegetation layer's lod_range/lod_fade_margin (data/config/vegetation.json) to its Terrain3DMeshAsset, which Terrain3D turns into a real RenderingServer.instance_geometry_set_visibility_range on the MultiMeshes that layer draws. DEFAULT FALSE, which is exactly what shipped before PERF-ROG: measured with tools/perf_render_stats.gd on four elevated views, the AUTHORED ranges (110-260m) change draw calls by less than measurement noise, and FORCING every range to 20m -- culling everything past twenty metres, which no player would accept -- removes only 5-16%. The lever works; it is just not where the frames are. Left wired and gated rather than commented out so the next lane measures instead of re-deriving. Numbers in ralph/PERF_ROG_REPORT.md.
_comment_scatter_lod_vp3: VP3 (visual parity, VEG lane, 2026-09-02): TRUE. The PERF-ROG measurement above was taken with the authored ranges at 110-260m on the four elevated views, where almost nothing in frame was beyond 260m anyway -- which is why it moved nothing. The ranges in vegetation.json are now authored for this flag being on: canopy layers reach 700-800m so the horizon keeps its tree masses, and the ground layers (groundmat 90, drygrass 110, bushes 160) cull where a 0.5m plant is sub-pixel. Measured with tools/perf_render_stats.gd --views=band1_open,village_high,hall_approach --settle=120 --resettle=60 --sample=20, both states, in ralph/reports/visual-parity/VEG/REPORT.md.
_comment_scatter_lod_vp2: VP2 (visual parity program, 2026-09-02 05:50 UTC): FALSE, measured. With the grass carpet cull-tiled and main's owner density, tools/perf_render_stats.gd --settle=120 --resettle=60 --sample=20 at band1_open read 12.22M primitives / 7839 draw calls with this true and 11.80M / 7511 with it false; hall_approach 4270 vs 3975 draw calls. The visibility-range fade keeps both ends of each fade band resident, which costs more than the far cull saves in this world. Off meets every budget in docs/VISUAL_PARITY_PROGRESS.md. Numbers in ralph/reports/visual-parity/VP2-perf/.
_comment_overlay: debug_overlay_on_boot turns the F3 performance readout on from the first frame, for a device the owner cannot press F3 on: the ROG Ally is a handheld, and the owner's authored controller map (2026-08-22) spends every pad button on a gameplay verb with held chords banned, so there is no spare press to give this and a config flag is the honest answer rather than a colliding binding. Flip it, build, play, photograph the readout. debug_overlay_level: 1 = frame time, draw calls and the top three measured costs (scripts/world/perf_trace.gd); 2 = that plus movement and input diagnostics. F3 still cycles it on a keyboard.
_comment_structure_visibility_range: WORLD lane, band1_open over-budget follow-up (2026-09-02): 7659 draws / 7500 budget at band1_open, and tools/perf_render_stats.gd's own per-node breakdown puts 4058 of those on discrete built structures/props, not the grass carpet (133 MultiMesh draws total, already ruled out) or Terrain3D's own scatter (RenderingServer resources, not attributable). `scripts/world/structure_visibility_range.gd::apply()` reads this block and sets a real `GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_end`/`_end_margin` on a built group's own descendants (never on vegetation -- it skips any node whose name contains `skip_name_contains`, which is what keeps village.gd's square_oak_a/b settlement trees and burrow_warrens.gd's Bush_Common/Grass_Wide_Tall/Plant_1 skirt flora untouched even though they stand inside a 'structures' group). Gated by `structure_visibility_ranges` (false by default, mirroring `scatter_lod_ranges` above) AND each distance itself must be > 0 -- either being off/absent is a complete no-op, so nothing changes until an owner turns this on. `default` covers Village (mixed cottage/workshop massing, common wall-top height ~3m + roof to a ~5m ridge -- the kit's own recipe geometry in building_prefabs.json) and anything with no group-specific override; the `groups` map overrides that per named group where the group's own object scale differs. Distances are derived, not fitted: 70deg vertical FOV over 540px (VP_FAST) gives 1 degree ~= 7.7px, so an object of height h at distance d subtends h/d radians = (h/d)*(180/pi) degrees ~= (h/d)*441.8 px; solved for d at a 3px cull threshold (a target picked to sit close to this repo's own precedent -- vegetation.json's ground-cover LOD ranges land at ~2px for a 0.5m plant -- but a little looser, because a rectilinear building silhouette reads at a smaller apparent size than a single blade of grass before it stops contributing) that is d = h * 147.3. Stronghold is DELIBERATELY ABSENT from `groups` and NEVER receives a call to `apply()` at all -- CLAUDE.md's landmark-silhouette rule: the works/keep/towers are the wayfinding spine's own landmark and stay drawn at any distance the game can already see them from. Per-group reasoning: `props` (h~2m ground clutter -- crates, campfires, fence posts) -> d=294m, rounded to 300; `village_boundary` (h~1.7m two-course fence run per village_boundary.gd's own course_rise*courses arithmetic, corner posts taller at +CORNER_EXTRA_HEIGHT_M but a small fraction of the run) -> d=250m, rounded up to 450 to keep even the tallest corner posts (~4.5m) legible past their own ~660m point; `grandpa_house` (h~9m, the settlement's one bespoke two-storey building -- FLOOR_H+LOFT_H alone is 6.1m before the roof) -> d=1326m, rounded to 1300; `burrow_warrens` (its own comments describe the exterior as 'a rock knoll with a hole in it', h~7m estimated) -> d=1031m, rounded to 1000; `mill_crossing` (bridge/mill massing, h~7m estimated) -> d=1031m, rounded to 1000; `severed_spokes` (blocker debris -- rockslide blocks, sealed-road walls -- wall_height/ROCK_MODEL_HEIGHT constants in severed_spokes.gd run 2.2-4.2m, h~3.5m) -> d=515m, rounded to 500. `village` itself takes no override and falls back to `default` (700m): it mixes ~5m single-storey cottages with two rare ~9-10m outliers (the mill, the inn), and one group-wide range cannot serve both -- sized to the PREDOMINANT scale rather than the outliers, which is a known, stated simplification (the mill and the inn will fade a little earlier than their own individual 3px point would justify) rather than an unstated one. Full reasoning, the group-by-group camera-distance table this was checked against, and the honest accounting of which of these groups actually sit ahead of band1_open's own camera (which faces -Z, back toward the village, per perf_render_stats.gd's own VIEWS comment -- Stronghold/BurrowWarrens/MillCrossing and most of SeveredSpokes' seven routes sit at WORLD +z, i.e. behind that specific stand's camera) are recorded in the WORLD lane's own report, not repeated here.
